quizName: DMV Practice Test #14 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What color is a warning sign with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert drivers to hazards or road conditions ahead.

questions.question: How can you reduce your reaction time?

options.text: Ride slower than the speed limit.
Cover the clutch and the brakes.
Pull in the clutch when turning.

questions.correctAnswerText: Cover the clutch and the brakes.
questions.explanation: Keep your hands ready over the clutch and brakes. This reduces reaction time, especially in areas where hazards may appear.

questions.question: When riding a three-wheel motorcycle in a group, what formation should you use?
questions.explanation: Three-wheel motorcycles are too wide for a staggered formation. Ride in a single-file line instead.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, which adjustment is NOT needed?
questions.explanation: A passenger adds weight, so adjust tire pressure, mirrors, and headlight. The brake light position does not need adjustment.

questions.question: What type of footwear is proper for motorcycle riding?
questions.explanation: Wear sturdy footwear that covers your ankles. Short heels are best because tall heels can catch on things. Keep laces tucked in so they don't get caught.

questions.question: How much stopping power does the front brake provide?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake and provides about 70 percent of total stopping power.

questions.question: If your rear wheel locks while braking, what should you do?

options.text: Release the brake until the rear tire regains traction, then re-apply the brake.
Release the brake and only engage the front brake.
Keep it locked until the motorcycle comes to a stop.
Release the brake and coast to a stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep it locked until the motorcycle comes to a stop.
questions.explanation: If your rear wheel locks, do not release the brake. Keep it locked until you stop completely.

questions.question: Under ideal conditions, what is the minimum following distance?
questions.explanation: Keep at least two seconds between you and the vehicle ahead under normal conditions. Increase this distance if conditions are worse.

questions.question: When turning, how should you look through the turn?

options.text: Turn your head and shoulders to look through turns.
Keep your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn just your head and eyes to look through turns.
questions.explanation: Look through a turn to where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon.

questions.question: When braking on a slippery surface, which brake should you use?

options.text: Use both the front and rear brakes.
Use abrupt pressure on the front brake to prevent locking the front tire.
Use either brake, but use only one brake.

questions.correctAnswerText: Use both the front and rear brakes.
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, use both brakes. Squeeze the front brake lever slowly to avoid locking the front wheel and use gentle pressure on the rear brake.

questions.question: When looking through a turn, you should:

options.text: Turn both your head and shoulders.
Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
Move only your eyes, not your head.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head, not your shoulders.
questions.explanation: Look through the turn toward where you want to go. Turn your head only, keep your shoulders still, and keep your eyes level.

questions.question: A motorcycle passenger should:

options.text: Get on before the engine starts.
Get on after the engine starts.
Sit as far back as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on after the engine starts.
questions.explanation: Get on a motorcycle only after the engine starts and the transmission is in neutral. Sit as far forward as you can without blocking the driver's control. Hold onto the driver's waist, hips, or belt.

questions.question: Fatigue while riding can be increased by:

options.text: Riding in cool, windy, or rainy weather.
Starting a ride late in the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Riding in cool, windy, or rainy weather.
questions.explanation: Dress to protect yourself from bad weather. Limit riding to about six hours per day. Take a break at least every two hours. Do not use artificial stimulants because you will become very tired when they wear off.

questions.question: When turning left, you should:

options.text: Press both handgrips at the same time.

questions.explanation: A motorcycle must lean to turn. Press the handgrip in the direction you want to turn to make the motorcycle lean the right way.

questions.question: When a driver's left arm is bent at the elbow and pointing upward, it means the driver:
questions.explanation: Drivers use hand signals when they don't have mechanical turn signals. A bent left arm pointing up means the driver plans to turn right or move right.

questions.question: Because of their small size, motorcycles seem to be:

options.text: Traveling faster than they actually are.
Traveling slower than they actually are.
Not moving when they actually are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traveling faster than they actually are.
questions.explanation: Because motorcycles are small, they look like they are going faster than they really are.

questions.question: The two main types of helmets are:
questions.explanation: The two main helmet types are three-quarter and full-face. Full-face helmets offer the most protection.

questions.question: Which of the following helps you ride safely on slippery surfaces?
questions.explanation: On slippery surfaces, slow down, use both brakes, and avoid sudden moves. Stay away from the center lane and follow tire tracks left by other vehicles. Watch for hazards like oil spots and loose gravel.

questions.question: Before riding, make sure the fuel supply valve:
questions.explanation: Open the fuel supply valve before you ride. If it is closed, the engine may start using old fuel in the lines but will stall when that fuel runs out.

questions.question: A linked braking system:

options.text: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes apply when either lever is used.
Connects the front brake to the gear shifter to apply the brake when downshifting.
Connects the rear brake to a foot control.
Connects the rear brake to a handlebar switch.

questions.correctAnswerText: Connects the front and rear brakes so both brakes apply when either lever is used.
questions.explanation: A linked braking system connects the front and rear brakes. When you use either brake, both brakes apply at the same time. Check your owner's manual for details about your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: What should you use when riding in rain or fog?

options.text: Switch between low and high beams

questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in rain, snow, or fog. High beam headlights reflect off these conditions and make it harder to see.

questions.question: How long before turning or changing lanes must you signal?
questions.explanation: Utah law requires you to signal at least two seconds before you turn or change lanes.

questions.question: How often should you check your motorcycle's hydraulic fluid at minimum?
questions.explanation: Check hydraulic fluid and coolant at least once a week as part of your regular motorcycle maintenance for safe riding.

questions.question: Where should you ride in your lane when another vehicle is passing you?
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane when being passed. Riding too close to the passing vehicle increases collision risk. Riding too far away may encourage the driver to re-enter your lane unsafely.

questions.question: How can you increase the chances of other drivers seeing you at an intersection?
questions.explanation: Keep your headlight on at intersections. Ride in a position where oncoming traffic can easily see you. Keep a safe space cushion to avoid danger. Do not assume another driver sees you, even with eye contact.
